entry.title: Sleep Countdown Reset 1.0.0
entry.content:
Sleep Countdown Reset

Media servers such as Plex keep the PC awake while streaming, but idle time still accumulates. When playback ends and the request is released, Windows checks the expired idle time and sleeps immediately, leaving no time to start the next episode/media/exchange.

This mod hooks the keep-awake APIs inside each server process. Right before the server releases the request, the mod takes over with its own, for a configurable grace period or, by default, the active power plan's sleep timeout. After this period, if playback does not return, the PC sleeps normally.

Display timer and monitor state stay under Windows' control. While the grace period runs, powercfg /requests lists the mod's request under SYSTEM.

Supported servers

Included by default:

  • Plex Media Server
  • Emby Server (EmbyServer.exe)
  • Jellyfin (jellyfin.exe): only with the third-party Prevent Sleep plugin, since Jellyfin alone doesn't keep the PC awake. On PCs with Modern Standby the plugin switches power plans instead, which this mod can't see.

Can be added (see below):

  • Universal Media Server: javaw.exe, with its "Prevent sleep" option set to Playback. That process name is shared by every Java program, so they all get the grace period.
  • qBittorrent (qbittorrent.exe), with "Inhibit system sleep" enabled: grace period after downloads finish.

Not needed: remote desktop and game streaming hosts (Sunshine, Parsec, Steam Remote Play). They forward the remote keyboard and mouse as local input, so Windows already counts the user as present.

Not covered: Windows file sharing (SMB). It runs inside the kernel, with no process to hook.

Adding a program

  1. While the program is serving, run powercfg /requests in a terminal as administrator. The program must be listed under SYSTEM or EXECUTION.
  2. In Windhawk, open this mod's Advanced tab, add the executable name (e.g. qbittorrent.exe) to the custom process inclusion list, and save.
  3. With debug logging enabled, the log should show hooked SetThreadExecutionState for the new process. If the program runs as a Windows service and nothing shows up, check that Windhawk is allowed to inject into services.

Limitation

If the server process exits while holding the request, Windows drops it without any API call, and the mod can't see the release.

entry.title: Mutelith 1.0
entry.content:
Mutelith

Fixes Discord double audio when screen sharing on Windows setups that use virtual audio devices, where viewers hear the game or desktop audio twice, or hear their own microphone coming back with a delay.

Provider Target device (Discord muted)
SteelSeries Sonar SteelSeries Sonar - Microphone
FxSound FxSound Speakers

The provider is detected from the default output device.

While Discord is running, the mod:

  1. Mutes Discord on the provider's target device and on every device outside the provider (speakers, headphones). Only the mute changes, never the volume.
  2. Leaves the provider's other virtual devices alone.
  3. When the mod is disabled, or the default device switches to another provider, unmutes Discord on the devices the rule no longer covers.

With FxSound, FxSound Speakers is usually the only FxSound device, so every other output device is outside the provider and Discord is muted on all of them, voice chat included.

It reacts to Windows audio notifications right away (default device changed, device added or removed, new audio session such as a screen share, a muted session was unmuted) and also checks every 30 seconds.

Windows remembers the mute

The mute is Discord's per-app setting in the Volume Mixer, and Windows saves it for each output device, so it outlives the mod. The mod records each device it muted Discord on and unmutes Discord there once the rule no longer covers it, including after a crash. Windows only lets the mod do that while Discord is running and to have an audio session on that device. If Discord isn't listed for a device in the Volume Mixer when you disable the mod, Discord stays muted there: open the Volume Mixer and unmute Discord, or enable the mod again while Discord is playing audio on that device and switch the default device away from the provider. A mute you set yourself in the Volume Mixer is left alone.

Mutelith app

This is the same rule as the Mutelith app. Use one or the other: while Mutelith.exe is running, the mod does nothing.

Designed and tested for one virtual audio provider at a time.

entry.title: OSD Custom Pill 4.9.11
entry.content:
OSD Custom Pill

An animated on-screen indicator for volume, brightness and virtual desktops on Windows 11.

Volume and brightness

Shows an icon, a progress bar and the current value. The indicator expands when it appears and retracts when it closes.

Elastic deformation

Increasing a value moves and stretches the pill to the right; decreasing it moves the pill to the left. Repeated changes build up the deformation. When you release the key, the pill returns with a spring effect.

The movement, stretching, spring damping and return strength can be adjusted independently in the mod settings.

Compact mode

After several changes in a row, the indicator can become smaller to take up less space. You can choose how many changes activate this mode and when it returns to normal.

Size and position

Adjust the pill's width, height and distance from the bottom of the screen. Opening and closing delays can also be changed.

Virtual desktops

Displays the current virtual desktop name or number when switching desktops. This indicator has its own size, position, animation and duration settings.

Settings

All options are available in Windhawk's Settings tab, with translated labels in supported languages. The main groups are:

Appearance and position — dimensions and screen placement.

Opening and closing — delays and spring response.

Stretching and rebound — movement distance, deformation and elastic return.

Compact mode — activation threshold and return timing.

Virtual desktop indicator — label, dimensions, timing and animation.

Timing values are in milliseconds. Size values are based on 100% display scaling.

entry.title: Arabic Keyboard Layout Fixer 1.3.0
entry.content:
Arabic Keyboard Layout Fixer

Fixes the common frustration of typing Arabic text while the keyboard is accidentally set to English (or vice versa).

How to use:

  1. Select/highlight any mistyped text in any app (Notepad, Word, Browser, ERP, etc.).
  2. Press Alt + Z (or your custom configured hotkey).
  3. The text instantly flips to the correct language!

Features:

  • Bi-directional (AR <-> EN): Automatically detects language direction.
  • Smart Shift / Caps Lock fix: Resolves accidental Shift / Caps-Lock misfires.
  • Configurable hotkeys: Customize your hotkey from mod settings without conflicts.
  • Universal compatibility: Works in modern browsers, Office, and legacy Win32/ERP applications.
  • Dedicated tool process: Runs safely as an independent background tool mod.
  • Full clipboard preservation: Restores all clipboard formats (images, files, text) and keeps history clean.

entry.title: Explorer Translucent Menus 1.0.2
entry.content:
Explorer Translucent Menus

Apply translucent materials to classic Win32 popup menus in File Explorer. Windows continues to provide menu items, layout, commands, keyboard navigation, and shell extensions. Windows 11's modern context menu is left unchanged.

This is an Explorer-only, menu-focused alternative to the archived TranslucentFlyouts project. It covers classic popup menus hosted by explorer.exe, including desktop and File Explorer context menus. It leaves the main Explorer window background, ordinary controls, and other processes unchanged.

Screenshots

Materials in light and dark themes

Tint and transparency adjustments

Borders and submenus

Requirements

  • Windows 11 22H2 or later (build 22621+), 64-bit.
  • Desktop composition and Windows transparency effects enabled.
  • No other renderer modifying the same Explorer menus.

To open a classic context menu on Windows 11, select Show more options or use Shift+F10. Select Native to disable all hooks. For a temporary bypass, enable Hold Ctrl to bypass in the settings, then hold Ctrl before opening a menu.

Materials

Material Tint opacity
Native No modifications
Solid Always opaque
Transparent Adjustable, no blur
Acrylic Adjustable tint over blur
Modern Acrylic Adjustable tint color, fixed opacity
System Acrylic Fixed Windows recipe
Mica / Mica Alt Fixed Windows recipes

Tint opacity changes the material, not text or icons. Theme selection controls the light or dark palette. Hover highlight opacity can be adjusted separately. Unrecognized saved material values use Acrylic.

Appearance

Enable Hide menu border to suppress the outline on modified menus. This preserves menu dimensions and works with rounded or square corners. Native mode and Ctrl bypass retain the complete Windows appearance. The option also protects the outline setting from later Shell/UxTheme updates while the modified menu is being tracked.

Legacy icon repair converts copied RGB bitmaps to premultiplied alpha. Optional background removal clears only matching corner-connected white, black, or magenta regions. Disable background removal for icons with intentional borders. Transfers that declare per-pixel alpha, and bitmaps with ambiguous partial alpha, retain the original GDI behavior. The mod does not guess whether an existing alpha bitmap is straight or premultiplied.

Scope and rendering approach

This mod keeps the Shell's immersive owner-draw enabled and preserves native menu layout, commands, and shell extensions. Effects are scoped to supported classic popups while a menu is tracked. Preparation validates resources before applying effects and exposes the popup to drawing hooks only after commit. Only successful state changes are recorded for cleanup. Unassociated memory DCs are left to Windows; owner-draw memory DCs require an exact synchronous WM_DRAWITEM match. GDI and UxTheme hooks are installed in Explorer, but forward to Windows outside a tracked menu. The scope is the popup effect, rather than a replacement for Explorer's overall interface rendering.

Translucent Windows and Win32 UI Modernizer already offer translucent classic menus. Translucent Windows shares background-effect configuration between windows and flyouts, with menu drawing integrated into its broader theme-rendering path. Win32 UI Modernizer lets users disable its Explorer section and other general features, but its modern menu modes disable immersive owner-draw and also modernize ComboBox dropdowns.

The purpose of this separate implementation is to provide a dedicated popup renderer that retains the Shell's owner-draw path and can accompany a separate Explorer background renderer. Restricting process targets or adding material presets alone does not provide that rendering behavior. An equivalent mode in a broader UI mod would need to isolate menu rendering and preserve immersive owner-draw as well.

Compatibility

Menu effects from these mods conflict when enabled on the same Explorer popups:

  • Translucent Windows: Flyout effects also renders classic menus, dropdowns, and tooltips. Disable that option to remove its flyout effects.
  • Win32 UI Modernizer: set Menus and dropdowns to Native (no modernization). Both modern modes apply their own acrylic rendering and disable immersive owner-draw.

These settings turn off their direct menu features. Their remaining Explorer effects and shared drawing hooks depend on other settings, so compatibility must be evaluated with the configuration in use. To avoid their remaining hooks in Explorer while continuing to use them in other applications, exclude explorer.exe from their targets in Windhawk's Advanced tab.

This mod is also compatible with ExplorerBlurMica, which supplies the main Explorer window backdrop. This mod keeps its effects confined to classic popup menus and leaves the main window backdrop to ExplorerBlurMica.

Unknown owner-drawn menus, custom background brushes, high contrast, remote sessions, disabled transparency, and recognized conflicting renderers are left unchanged. Settings changes reload the mod. Menu opening animations follow the Windows settings and the caller's flags, including when effects are active.

Menus whose previous system-backdrop value cannot be read stay native. Unreadable optional dark-mode and corner preferences are left unchanged. Recorded values are restored on live-window cleanup; failed restores remain pending for retry. There are no public getters for prior blur regions or extended-frame margins, and the Accent getter is unavailable on some builds. Cleanup of those states is best-effort, not a lossless restoration guarantee for an unknown renderer. A missing border-color snapshot likewise uses the Windows default on cleanup. Destroyed popup HWNDs release their window-owned effects without extra resets.

The implementation uses version-dependent Windows interfaces: the composition attribute exports, UxTheme ordinal 74, the DarkMode::Menu theme, menu layout message 0x1e2, and Shell window properties. It does not read private Shell item structures, patch instructions, download symbols, or replace the menu loop.

Troubleshooting

Enable log output in Windhawk's Advanced tab to record menu preparation, material and border application results, native fallback reasons, and cleanup. There is no separate logging setting in this mod. Native mode registers no menu hooks, so it reports initialization rather than individual menu openings.

Credits and license

Informed by TranslucentFlyouts, Translucent Windows, and Custom Cached Context Menu. This implementation is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later.

entry.title: Outlook Refined 0.6.2
entry.content:
• Credit the author in the readme, with a link to their site.
  • Align the agenda and its divider with the favorites list above them. The agenda was positioned against the navigation pane while the list sits inside Outlook's own scrolling container, so the two halves of the pane never shared an edge.
  • Give the folder names back 18px. The element holding the folder tree reserves a scrollbar gutter while its own overflow is hidden, so nothing is ever drawn in it; releasing the reservation takes the pane from 163px of usable width to 181px on a 197px pane and leaves 8px on both sides.

entry.title: Taskbar Fluent Media Player 1.7.0
entry.content:
The big ones

  • Its own settings window. Right-click the player and pick Settings. It's built in the Windows 11 style with Mica, sorted into pages, and changes show on the player while you make them. It comes in 15 languages and follows your Windows language by default.
  • Settings live in the mod now. The first time 1.7 runs, it copies everything from Windhawk's settings page, so you don't lose anything. Save keeps your changes, and closing only warns you if something really differs from what's saved.
  • Move any part of the player. Album art, track info, buttons and the visualizer can each be detached and placed somewhere else on the taskbar or tray, with their own background and monitor.
  • Progress bar. It can sit under any part of the player or the whole thing, on its own line or drawn on top. Click or drag it to seek.
  • Vertical taskbars. If yours is docked left or right, the text and album art turn to read along it and the buttons stack up.
  • Monitor buttons. Pick a monitor by clicking its button, numbered like Windows. Click the selected one again to hide the player. Monitors that aren't connected stay gray and become available when you plug them in.

Visualizer

  • "Only listen to the app in the player", on by default, so a Discord call or a game won't move the bars (Windows 11). (#93, #85)
  • New: it can fill the background behind the whole player.
  • New: Line style, and a Micro version that fits next to the artist text. (#16)
  • Pick which audio device it listens to, including recording devices. (#17, #50)
  • Hide it when nothing is playing. (#14)
  • Tune each of the 7 frequency bands.

Player and layout

  • Set the order of album art, text, buttons and visualizer. (#32)
  • "Media player offset" moves the player without making the taskbar wider, which helps with floating Taskbar Styler themes. (#88)
  • Reorder the media buttons and right-click menu items.
  • Hide the whole player while paused, after a delay you choose. (#14)
  • Hide the Windows Widgets button.

Text

  • Show the album name instead of the artist, or only when there's no cover. (#38)
  • Custom text formats with %title%, %artist%, %album% and %artist_or_album%. (#38)
  • Show the playback time (like 2:02/4:24) instead of the artist.
  • Hide the text when nothing is playing.

Clicks and apps

  • Choose an app to open when you click the player with nothing playing. (#23)
  • New click actions: minimize, open or minimize, and close the media app. (#53)
  • "Only show these apps" mode, and the app filter moved out of Debug into Behaviour. (#64)

Mini player

  • Seek bar, with its own color. (#62)
  • Background options: Acrylic, solid color, album colors gradient or blurred cover. (#48)
  • Corner radius setting, and the bottom icon row can be turned off. (#84)

Settings window extras

  • Choose the window's background: Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic or Acrylic Thin. Acrylic shows what's behind the window, so it works with live wallpapers that Mica can't see, and has its own transparency and blur sliders.
  • The title bar can match the window, stay as Windows draws it, or take any color.
  • The page fades at its top and bottom edges while you scroll.
  • Any color can follow the album, including the window's own accent, which fades to the new color when the song changes.
  • Report a bug from inside the window. You choose whether to attach errors, crash info, the log and your settings. Reports also include your PC name and Windows user name, and the form says so.
  • Reset to Windhawk's settings, in Other.
  • An Animations switch, which also follows Windows' own setting.

Fixes

Windows updates

  • Works again after the updates that changed the system tray and the September taskbar update. (#69, #78, #79, #83, #89, #91)
  • If the button the player sits next to doesn't exist on your build, the player goes to the start of the tray instead of disappearing.
  • The player no longer vanishes when Do Not Disturb is on.

Startup and stability

  • If the player doesn't make it onto the taskbar at startup, the mod tries again. (#67, #68, #73, #82)
  • Media keys keep working after an Explorer restart. (#52)
  • The player corrects itself if it ends up on the wrong side of its tray button.
  • Security report: fixes for callback handling, the shell32 and windhawk.exe lookups, image handling and unloading. (#71)

Which app it follows

  • The player stays on the app that's playing instead of a paused one. (#22)
  • It no longer flashes another app when tracks change. (#34)
  • Ignored apps stay out of session switching, and the ignore list also matches the browser's exe. (#66, #70, #77)

Album art and colors

  • Covers up to 24 MB show up. (#81)
  • Old art no longer stays when a browser track has none. (#33)
  • The Album color works on the progress bar, the visualizer and everything else, including with album art turned off.
  • With no album art, dynamic visualizer colors go back to your normal color. (#58)
  • Solid backgrounds survive switching between light and dark. (#57)

Visualizer

  • Keeps reacting when you switch the player to another app, like Clipchamp, Firefox or Snipping Tool.
  • Much lower GPU use when nothing is playing. (#41)

Monitors

  • Text scrolling and the visualizer keep working after the player moves to another monitor.

Input and placement

  • Pause works reliably in Zen browser. (#26)
  • Right and middle double-click actions fire again.
  • "Hide when no media" no longer keeps taking up space. (#14)
  • Fixed the gap with "Right of Widgets", and the player going under the icons with Taskbar Styler "Borderless". (#74)

Not in this version

  • Showing the player on several monitors at the same time is still planned. (#15, #90)

Thanks

  • Net-zen for the StackPanel tray patch (#87).
  • Everyone who reported bugs and tested the alphas on the Windhawk Discord.

entry.title: Mac OS 27 Finder Bar 1.0.0
entry.content:
Mac OS 27 Finder Bar

A Windhawk mod that adds a macOS 27-style menu bar to the top of the screen in Windows 11: the menus of the app in front on the left, and system status, Control Center, notifications and the clock on the right, all in live glass.

Available in English, Português, Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano and 中文（简体）. The language follows Windows automatically, or can be picked in the settings.

Left side

  • Logo menu: About This PC, System Settings, Microsoft Store (both with pending update counts), Force Quit, Show Desktop, Sleep, Hibernate, Restart, Shut Down, Lock Screen, Sign Out and Menu Bar Settings…
  • Active app name (shown as Finder for the desktop and File Explorer, a name you can change): hide the app, hide others, open file location, close window, quit, force quit
  • Global menu:
    • apps with a classic menu bar (Win32): the app's real menus
    • modern apps: the app's menu bar read through UI Automation when it exists
    • browsers, File Explorer, Office, VS Code and other apps: ready-made menus that send the app's own keyboard shortcuts
    • a Window menu with the app's open windows
  • Help menu with a search across all the app's menus; ← → move between menus (optional Ctrl+F2 opens the bar from the keyboard)

Right side

  • Display: dark mode, night light, projection modes
  • Keyboard layout (when there is more than one), emoji, on-screen keyboard
  • Battery (percentage, charging, time remaining), Wi-Fi (current network, available and known networks), Bluetooth and Sound (scroll on the icon to change the volume, right-click to mute, switch output and input)
  • Now Playing: the song name scrolls across the bar when it doesn't fit; the panel has a large-cover or compact layout and a progress bar drawn as a line, a colored line or a wave
  • Focus (when Do Not Disturb is on), Search (Windows Search or Siri Plus Launchpad), microphone and camera (the icons turn orange and green while an app uses them, as on the Mac; click to see which apps use them and mute the microphone), Weather (Open-Meteo, MET Norway or wttr.in, no account needed) and the Notifications button
  • Clock: the calendar and your agenda from your own .ics files, imported right from the settings window. Date and time formats are configurable
  • An arrow collapses the icons that don't fit; each icon can be turned on or off in the settings

Control Center

Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, media playing, dark mode, Do Not Disturb, brightness, sound and audio output, plus tiles you can add: night light, airplane mode, screenshot, screen recording, power mode, energy saver (one click turns it on and off), magnifier, lock screen, calculator, Task Manager, emoji and show desktop.

  • Edit Controls lets you add, remove, move and resize tiles
  • Clicking power mode opens a box under Edit Controls, as wide as the panel, with the Windows 11 power modes and power plans (repeated plans are hidden)
  • Tile names that don't fit scroll when the mouse is over the tile
  • Tiles can be pills or rounded squares; a tile that is on shows a colored circle or turns into a whole white pill
  • Optional: blur and dim the screen while the Control Center is open; cascade or fade animation when it opens

Notice pills

Small glass pills drop from the bar for headphones, audio output, low battery, charger, Focus, Caps Lock, USB devices and drives, finished downloads, copy and cut, screenshots and screen recordings. Pills you can act on (open and edit a screenshot or recording, open a download, reply to a message) stay 2.5 times longer and are kept in the bell panel; the rest only show in the pill. Volume, brightness and Bluetooth changes can show as floating pills too. The pill's style (glass, liquid glass or dark), size, position, duration and opening and closing animations are all configurable.

Notifications

Turn on Windows notifications in logo → Menu Bar Settings… → Notice pills (off by default) and the bar shows your apps' notifications:

  • in the pill and in the bell panel, grouped by app
  • reply to messages (like WhatsApp) right from the pill, when the app supports replies
  • drag a notification aside in the panel to clear it
  • Only the bar shows notifications: optional; Windows' own banners move off the screen while the bar shows them, and come back when the option or the mod is turned off

Bar and glass

  • Bar background: fully transparent (default), Windows blur glass, or liquid glass (experimental); opaque when the active app is maximized (optional)
  • Live glass: panels blur what's behind them in real time, with an experimental liquid glass with edge refraction (on by default)
  • Menus use their own frosted glass (with a transparency slider) or the same glass as the Control Center
  • Light, dark or automatic theme, nine selection colors for the bar and menus, font, font size, icon size and bar height
  • Hides with full-screen apps, can hide automatically until the mouse touches the top, and shows on every monitor (each optional)

Settings

Logo → Menu Bar Settings… opens a window in the same style as Siri Plus Launchpad: sections on the left with search, every setting applied live without restarting the bar. It's the only place for those settings. Windhawk's settings page has the few the window doesn't: font, glass tints, theme, the name shown for the desktop, ready-made menus, Control Center tile look, opening animation, tray click, the app update count and .ics file paths, plus Reset the bar's settings, which puts the window's options back to their defaults if the bar ever doesn't show up.

What changes Windows settings

Some Control Center tiles and menu items change real Windows settings, the same ones Windows' own quick settings change. They stay changed after the mod is turned off, as they would if you used Windows' quick settings:

  • Dark mode: the app and system light/dark theme (sets both to the same value)
  • Night light: on or off
  • Power mode and power plan: picking a power mode also switches the plan to Balanced, as Windows requires
  • Energy saver and Do Not Disturb
  • Brightness, default audio device, volume and mute, microphone mute, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios, Wi-Fi network and display mode (projection)

Nothing is changed unless you click the matching tile or item.

Network use

The mod only goes online for features you set up yourself (the calendar reads local .ics files only, never the network):

  • Weather, once you pick a place: the place search uses OpenStreetMap Nominatim or Open-Meteo, and the forecast comes from the service you choose (Open-Meteo, MET Norway or wttr.in) with the place's coordinates rounded to about 1 km. Turning the weather icon off stops all requests.
  • App update count (off by default, in Windhawk's settings): runs winget upgrade, which checks winget's sources online. The mod doesn't accept winget's source agreements for you. The Windows Update count is offline.

Privacy

The copy pill only says "Copied" or "Cut": it never shows what was copied, and it skips anything an app marks as private (password managers do), the same way Windows' clipboard history does.

How it runs

The bar runs in its own Windhawk process (shown as Windhawk in Task Manager), so if it ever fails, the taskbar and desktop keep working. Explorer keeps only a small hook that copies the tray icons' registrations to the bar. If that process is ended by hand, turn the mod off and on again in Windhawk to bring the bar back.

Known limitations

  • Apps without a classic menu bar use ready-made menus based on keyboard shortcuts.
  • Bluetooth lists classic (non-BLE) devices and opens Settings to connect and disconnect.
  • Power mode and energy saver use undocumented Windows functions; if Windows refuses, the tile opens the matching Settings page.
  • Screen recording uses Win+Shift+R and needs an up-to-date Snipping Tool.
  • Replying from the pill works with apps that register a notification activator with Windows; otherwise the pill opens the app and copies your text.
  • With live glass (and the bar's liquid background), the bar and panels don't show up in screenshots.
  • If Windhawk itself runs as administrator (portable mode started elevated), the bar doesn't show the tray icons: letting the shell's tray data reach an elevated bar would also let any app send it fake icons.
